correctness.rationale: For proper subspaces \(U,W\) of a finite vector space, \(U\le W\) implies \(N(U)\subseteq N(W)\). If \(U\not\le W\), a hyperplane containing \(W\) but excluding one vector of \(U\) is a neighbor of \(U\) and not of \(W\), proving the converse. Thus graph automorphisms recover the full subspace order. The fundamental theorem of projective geometry yields \(\operatorname{PGL}(d,p)\) because the base field is prime. In rank three the point-plane block matrix is exact; the identities \(MM^{\mathsf T}=pI+J\) and \(BB^{\mathsf T}=pI+p(p-1)J\) split the spectrum into one two-dimensional all-ones block and \(p^2+p\) identical two-dimensional orthogonal blocks. The packaged checker verifies the graph, incidence identities, order reconstruction, and spectral polynomial identity for \(p=2,3,5\).

value.rationale: Lucchini explicitly frames join-graph isomorphism as a problem of recovering group structure. The automorphism theorem resolves the self-isomorphism version completely for every elementary-abelian rank at least three: all graph symmetries are the expected projective linear symmetries, and the graph determines the prime and rank inside this family. Rank three is the first noncomplete elementary-abelian case, so its exact projective-plane spectrum is a natural base case rather than an arbitrary slice. The factorization gives immediate integral-algebraic control of the spectrum and a closed energy formula, while the rank-two boundary explains why the rigidity threshold is sharp.
